newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil-Stable with sporadic Chinese imports.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil-Stable with sporadic Chinese imports.

text.p: Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market were stable on Monday amid sporadic imports from China, traders said.
They said any rise in prices caused by reduced Middle East exports is expected to be capped by weak regional demand.

Enquiries were heard from Chinese buyers at $102-$103 per tonne, or at around $6-$7 per tonne premia to Singapore spot quotes on a cost-and-freight South China basis. Offers were at least $8 per tonne premia, traders said.
Traders said Chinese buyers in Shanghai and Guangdong have also been enquiring for medium sulphur supplies (1.5-2.0 percent) instead of the previous high sulphur grades (3.5 percent).
Traders said enviromental concerns have caused provincial authorities in Shanghai to pass a law requiring imports to be of medium sulphur.
In southern China, power companies concerned that high sulphur supplies would caused rapid corrosions on power plants have also decided to switch to medium sulphur grade fuel oil, traders said.
Chinese buyers were not concerned on a lack of supplies of medium sulphur grades, citing increased exports from Russia.
"There are alot more exports of the Russion M100 currently," said a Chinese importer in Singapore.

Outside China, buying interest were restricted to a local trader who up until last week has been keeping prices supported. The trader has so far purchased at least five cargoes in the past two week. The trader was believed to be bringing the cargoes to Indonesia, some traders said.
Late Monday, bids/offers in the benchmark Singapore market were quoted at $101.00/$101.25 for late June or early July supplies. But no trade was reported done.
Traders said Indonesia is also expected to buy more for July as a 200,000 bpd refinery crude unit at its Balikpapan refinery is scheduled to shut for a one-month maintenance.
A major said two Mideast cargoes were offered in the market but details of asking prices were unclear. Another Mideast cargo was also heard to be loading from Kuwait starting today, traders said.
The fuel oil swaps market slips lower higher amid thin talk and a lack of fresh demand in the cash market.
June swaps was quoted at $100.25/$101.25 from $101.00/$101.50 and July were at $99.50/$100.50 against $00.00/$100.75.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
